fields.description: The service-account key the CRM signs its push calls with, from Firebase: Project Settings → Service accounts → Generate new private key. Paste the JSON on one line, or its base64. It is stored encrypted, and the project id is read from inside it — there is no separate field for it.
fields.label: Firebase Service Account JSON

fields.description: Public Firebase web-app config the browser SDK needs to register a device token. Not secret (ships in client code). Project Settings → General → Your apps (Web).
fields.label: Browser (the rep's browser registers for push)
Web API Key
fields.description: From Firebase: Project Settings → General → Your apps → Web. Public by design — it ships in the browser and identifies the project; it grants nothing on its own.

fields.label: Auth Domain
fields.description: The same Web app config, field authDomain, e.g. my-project.firebaseapp.com.

fields.label: Project ID
fields.description: The same Web app config, field projectId. It must name the same Firebase project as the service account above.

fields.label: Messaging Sender ID
fields.description: The same Web app config, field messagingSenderId — the numeric sender the browser registers against.

fields.label: Web App ID
fields.description: The same Web app config, field appId.
The public key of the Web Push certificate pair, from Firebase: Cloud Messaging → Web configuration → Key pair. Without it a browser cannot be issued a device token, so no rep receives a push.
fields.label: VAPID Key (Web Push certificate)
